author: Carina Branson
title: 7-year-old Augusta cancer survivor living normal life - NewsBreak
text:
WICHITA, Kan. (KSNW) – Today, we are sharing the mission of the St. Jude Children’s Research Hospital . The hospital provides care to children battling cancer and other diseases without ever sending families a bill for their services. St. Jude is committed to continuing its research and treatment until no child dies from cancer.
When the hospital opened in 1962, the overall survival rate of childhood cancer was just 20 percent. Today it is 80 percent. St. Jude treats families from across the globe, including those from Wichita and throughout Kansas. Jessie is one of those patients. In July 2020, when Jessie was two, her family in Augusta learned she had a rare liver cancer. Searching for answers, St. Jude helped them figure out the next steps. Everything the family needed was taken care of and paid for by St. Jude, allowing the family to focus their energy on Jessie’s fight. “As soon as we got there, Jessie and I were wheeled into the hospital, and we were just met with, like, a team of doctors right away. They immediately told us, like, what the game plan would be from there. She actually got started on treatment that night. As soon as we got to St. Jude, they just immediately took care of us,” Annie, Jessie’s mom, said. Jessie is now 7 years old, five years since her diagnosis, and she is living a normal life.
